intro: Real numbers are made up of rational numbers (which can be written as p/q) and irrational numbers (which cannot). Every real number has a unique point on the number line. Rational numbers have terminating or repeating decimals; irrational numbers have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals.
keyPoints: Natural ⊂ Whole ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational ⊂ Real numbers.
Rational: p/q with p, q integers and q ≠ 0. Examples: 3, −2/5, 0.75, 0.333…
Laws of exponents: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, a⁰ = 1.
To rationalise 1/(a + √b), multiply top and bottom by (a − √b).
